sections.name: body
sections.value:
# Reviewer lessons: identity guards, lexical proof and CI freshness

Async selection is not mutation authority. #168 first filtered holdings by merge time, then discarded their `from`; a release/reassignment before the writer could substitute a new holding. The repaired path pins project/role/instance/seat/from and checks the exact open row under the writer lock. Keep explicit release semantics distinct from automatic completion, preserve retries after writer refusal, and test both serial replay and a deterministic interleaving. Check committed documents and the store independently.

An ancestry-cache hit needs a current suffix, not just a live cached root. The H-M-S-P chain in #163 survives cached-prefix checks when M dies and S reparents while H remains alive. Fresh bounded walks with strict in-process readers avoid that unsound authority shortcut. Boundary indexes may cache lookup metadata, never authorization.

Rollback only what the attempt created. #169's failed replacement of a prior daemon's pipe must keep its matching marker; clearing it stranded an owned pipe as foreign. Preserve the unknown-foreign-pipe veto. Failed attaches need bounded retries and visible unknown state, not a per-tick census. Pane-ID reset depends on observed disappearance unless a server-generation key is tracked.

Observation identifiers are not trusted prompt text. #175 parses stored build/tree fields at render time against a closed grammar and renders only parsed, explicitly seat-reported identifiers. Output safety is not caller/source attestation, and unrelated old seat-id/role weaknesses stay separate. Bound malformed input before searches/splits, not merely after collecting components. Compiler-only environment markers must be scoped to cargo, not inherited by the daemon and its jobs.

Content markers should cover the actual committed roots, not repository commit age. Docs/skills changes outside the hashed extension roots do not imply stale code. Whole-directory trees are coarse; package and dirty working-tree bytes are outside that proof.

Lexical import checks have a proof ceiling. Exact `from "` / `import("` leads missed comments and line breaks. P5's multiline template interpolation was discarded before the computed-path check; P6's escaping directory prefix resolved to no file and disappeared. Preserve spans and fail on unresolved escaping literals. Require a failing outside positive control plus an allowed inside control. Current literal-root consistency is not complete dynamic-JavaScript/security proof; opaque or computed dependency changes need independent review and declared roots.

CI artifact names are not freshness identifiers. A rerun can leave multiple `junit-linux` reports; `gh run download --name` selected an older failed report while the latest job passed. Match the artifact ID in the successful job's upload log and inspect that report. Verify the test actually executed, not only overall green status.

The #178 wrapper binds only inside `tombstone_if_unchanged`, after both eligibility pane reads. A real store CAS refuses the changed snapshot and writes no tombstone; moving the bind before those reads would not prove the same race.

Request verdicts only when all known fixes are pushed and the head is final. Verify the remote head, keep the detached review worktree fixed, and send a new exact-head packet for any delta. Verdicts stay pinned to that head, go through `pij output`, and answer the correct role request. Read-only reviewers use matching CI and clearly attributed author-run mutations; no local shared-machine builds/tests, no node_modules symlinks, no hidden live probes. Distinguish correctness, security, cost, fixture prose and deployed-runtime proof.
